entries.reason: the release wires a progress to its parent when it is created, through the current progress, and gives an existing progress no way to be attached afterwards
entries.effect: the child is attached through a progress of the port's own that the release makes under the parent, and the port carries the child's fraction into it as the child changes, so the parent's fraction moves with the child as it does in the newest release; the child stays independent of the parent's counts, and a progress that was made under another progress by the release is not known to be a child, so it can be added a second time
entries.source: the host's own Foundation, held against the port by tests/backports/host/progress and read again on an iPhone 4S and an iPad 2 running 6.1.3 by tests/backports/device/progress.m

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer, not the newest release's computed one (such as 25% completed)

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer (not-a-number for a zero total), not the newest release's (0)

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer (a handler set on an already-cancelled progress is never called), not the newest release's (called at once)

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer (a parent that is not the current progress is accepted), not the newest release's (NSInvalidArgumentException)

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer (a parent does not count a finished implicit child's units), not the newest release's; the fraction does, either way

the host's Foundation, and Foundation of iOS 6.0 and 6.1.3 read on the emulator and two devices; carried below 6.0 by Foundation/NSProgress.m, matching the release's own answer (the pending units stay uncounted when no child was made from them), not the newest release's (counted as completed)
